_comment: Snowflake-specific: the SQL below only runs there. Another vendor gets its own datalake-<vendor>.json with the same keys and `when datalake.kind == <vendor>`.

facts.verify: one row; the account matches the connector's URL

facts.purpose: default compute the connector runs on

args.sql: select table_catalog || '.' || table_schema || '.' || table_name from snowflake.account_usage.tables where deleted is null and table_name ilike '%spend%' order by 1

facts.verify: `select count(*) from <table> where <date column> >= dateadd(day, -7, current_date)` is > 0 and the table has a per-user email column
facts.purpose: the org's Claude spend table (cost-report org mode)
facts.note: several candidates → ask the user which is the billed source; none → leave empty (private mode)

facts.verify: each of the eight roles (date, email, model, cost, input, output, cache_read, cache_write) maps to exactly one existing column; propose the mapping by name similarity and confirm the ambiguous ones with the user
facts.purpose: column roles of the spend table

facts.verify: the tool is in this session's roster and answers `select 1`; the value is the tool name as the roster shows it (without the connector prefix)
facts.purpose: the warehouse's SQL MCP tool cost-report and pr-review call
facts.note: another vendor's connector has another tool name — it lives in that vendor's datalake-<vendor>.json
